spots.name: Bratislava Castle
spots.summary: Bratislava Castle is the main castle of Bratislava, the capital of Slovakia. The massive rectangular building with four corner towers stands on an isolated rocky hill of the Little Carpathians, directly above the Danube river, in the middle of Bratislava.

spots.name: St Martin's Cathedral, Bratislava
spots.summary: St Martin's Cathedral is a church in Bratislava, Slovakia, and the cathedral of the Archdiocese of Bratislava.

spots.name: Most SNP
spots.summary: Most SNP, commonly referred to as Most Slovenského národného povstania or the UFO Bridge, and named Nový most from 1993 to 2012, is a road bridge over the Danube in Bratislava, the capital of Slovakia. It is the world's longest bridge to have one pylon and one cable-stayed plane.

spots.name: Grassalkovich Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Grassalkovich Palace is a palace in Bratislava, Slovakia, and the residence of the President of Slovakia. It is situated on Hodžovo Square, near the Episcopal Summer Palace. The building is a Rococo summer palace with a French garden.

names.ja: グラッシャルコヴィチ宮殿

spots.name: Čumil
spots.summary: The Čumil statue, also known as Čumil the sewage worker, Man at work or simply Čumil, is a statue located in the city centre of Bratislava, the capital city of Slovakia. Čumil is considered one of the most prominent statues in Bratislava and is considered as one of the main attractions in the city center.

spots.name: Blue Church
spots.summary: The Church of St. Elizabeth, commonly known as Blue Church, is a Hungarian-Secessionist Catholic church located in the eastern part of the Old Town in Bratislava, present-day Slovakia. It is consecrated to Elisabeth of Hungary, daughter of Andrew II, who grew up in the Pressburg Castle (Pozsonyi vár).

spots.name: Michael's Gate
spots.summary: In Bratislava, Slovakia, Michael's Gate is the only city gate that has been preserved of the medieval fortifications and ranks among the oldest town buildings in Bratislava, Slovakia. Built about the year 1300, its present shape is the result of baroque reconstructions in 1758, when the statue of St.

spots.name: Primate's Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Primacial Palace is a neoclassical palace in the Old Town of Bratislava the capital of Slovakia. It was built from 1778 to 1781 for Archbishop of Esztergom József Batthyány, Primate of the Kingdom of Hungary, after the design of architect Melchior Hefele.

spots.name: Slavín
spots.summary: Slavín is a memorial monument and military cemetery in Bratislava, the capital of Slovakia.

spots.name: Hlavné námestie
spots.summary: Hlavné námestie is one of the best known squares in Bratislava, Slovakia. It is located in the Old Town and it is often considered to be the center of the city.

spots.name: Old Town Hall

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Old Town Hall is a complex of buildings from the 14th century in the Old Town of Bratislava, the capital of Slovakia. It is the oldest city hall in the country and it is one of the oldest stone buildings still standing in Bratislava, with the tower being built approximately in 1370.

names.zh: 布拉提斯拉瓦舊市政廳

spots.name: Franciscan Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Franciscan Church is the oldest existing religious (sacral) building in the Old Town of Bratislava, the capital of Slovakia. The church was consecrated in the year 1297 in the presence of King Andrew III of Hungary. In the past, the church building served for larger gatherings of townspeople or Hungarian nobles.

spots.name: Roland Fountain
spots.summary: The Roland Fountain is a Roland statue and among the most famous fountains in Bratislava, Slovakia. It is located on the Main Square of the Old Town.

spots.name: Starý most
spots.summary: Starý most is a bridge over the river Danube in Bratislava, Slovakia. The bridge was built as part of a railway project initiated by Hungarian retired general Gusztáv Dunst.

spots.name: Apollo Bridge
spots.summary: Apollo Bridge, provisionally known as Most Košická during construction after the street leading to it, in Bratislava is a road bridge over the Danube in the capital of Slovakia.

spots.name: Slovak National Gallery

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Slovak National Gallery is a network of galleries in Slovakia. It has its headquarters in Bratislava.

names.ja: スロバキア国立美術館

spots.name: Bratislava City Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Bratislava City Museum is a museum in Bratislava, Slovakia, established in 1868. Its headquarters are located in the Old Town, near the Main Square at the Old Town Hall. The museum is owned by one of the 11 allowance organizations of the City of Bratislava.

names.fr: Musée de la ville de Bratislava
names.es: Museo de la ciudad de Bratislava
names.zh: 布拉提斯拉瓦市博物館

spots.name: Universitas Istropolitana
spots.summary: The Universitas Istropolitana in Bratislava was arguably the third university to be found in the Kingdom of Hungary and the first university to be founded in the territory of present-day Slovakia. Despite its brief existence (1465–1491), it features prominently in Slovak historiography.

names.ja: イストロポリターナ大学

spots.name: Hviezdoslavovo námestie
spots.summary: Hviezdoslavovo námestie is a town square in Bratislava. It is located in the Old Town, between the Nový Most bridge and the Slovak National Theatre. The square is named after Pavol Országh Hviezdoslav.

spots.name: Námestie Slobody
spots.summary: Námestie Slobody , locally referred to as Gotko, is a major city square in the Old Town of Bratislava, the capital of Slovakia. It is situated in the wider city center, close to Kollárovo square and in front of the Summer Archbishop's Palace.

spots.name: Trinitarian Church of Bratislava

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Trinitarian Church or Trinity Church, full name Church of Saint John of Matha and Saint Felix of Valois, is a Baroque-style church in Bratislava's Old Town borough, on the Župné námestie square.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Old Cathedral of Saint John of Matha and Saint Felix of Valois

names.es: Catedral de San Juan de Mata y San Félix de Valois

spots.name: Statue of Svätopluk
spots.summary: Statue of Svätopluk is an equestrian bronze statue depicting Svätopluk, the third ruler of Great Moravia, located in the courtyard of Bratislava Castle in Bratislava, Slovakia. The creator of the statue is the Slovak sculptor Ján Kulich [sk].

spots.name: Eurovea Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Eurovea Tower is a premium high-rise residential skyscraper in Bratislava, Slovakia. The building was inaugurated in 2022 and stands at 168 metres (551 ft) tall, being divided into 45 floors. It is the tallest building in Slovakia and the first skyscraper over 150 m (490 ft) built in the country.

spots.name: Slovak National Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Slovak National Museum is the most important institution focusing on scientific research and cultural education in the field of museology in Slovakia. Its beginnings "are connected with the endeavour of the Slovak nation for national emancipation and self-determination".

names.ja: スロバキア国立博物館

spots.name: Jesuit Church, Bratislava

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Holy Saviour Church (Slovak: Kostol Najsvätejšieho Spasiteľa, also called Jezuitský kostol, or the Jesuit Church, is a church building constructed in the 17th century on Františkánske nám in the Old Town of Bratislava, Slovakia. It was originally built to serve as a protestant house of worship.

spots.name: St. Nicholas' Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St. Nicholas Church in Bratislava is an Orthodox church situated on the castle hill next to the Bratislava Castle in Podhradie the historical part of Bratislava, the capital of Slovakia. The church was built in 1661 by Paul Pálffy's (1589–1655) widow Countess Frances, née Khuen.

spots.name: Bratislava City Gallery

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Bratislava City Gallery is a gallery located in Bratislava, Slovakia, in the Old Town. It is the second largest Slovak gallery of its kind. The gallery is housed at the Mirbach Palace and Pálffy Palace.

names.ja: ブラチスラヴァ市ギャラリー
names.zh: 布拉提斯拉瓦市美術館

spots.name: Mirbach Palace
spots.summary: Mirbach Palace is a Baroque-Rococo building in the historical zone of Bratislava, Slovakia. The four-wing, two-story building, which ranks among the most beautiful and best-preserved architectural monuments of the mentioned style period in Slovakia, was named after the last owner, Baron Dr. Emil Mirbach.

spots.name: Clarissine Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Clarissine Church is a Gothic church, part of a complex of medieval buildings forming the former Convent of Poor Clares in the Old Town of Bratislava, the capital of Slovakia. The former Catholic church is owned by the city of Bratislava and it is used for cultural events.

spots.name: Esterházy Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Esterházy Palace is a Neo-Renaissance style building in the Old Town of Bratislava, Slovakia, near the Danube riverfront, built in the 1870s. The building was reconstructed in the 1920s and in the 1950s, when it was adapted for the Slovak National Gallery.

spots.name: SNP Square
spots.summary: Slovak National Uprising Square is a square in central Bratislava, Slovakia.

spots.name: Johann Pálffy Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Johann Pálffy Palace is a late Classicism-style building in the Old Town, Bratislava, Slovakia, on the Panská street, near the Hviezdoslav Square. The palace is standing on the site of a former building, which was until the mid-1850s the seat of Pozsony county.

spots.name: Zlaté Piesky
spots.summary: Zlaté Piesky is a lake and a summer resort in northeastern Bratislava, Slovakia, near the D1 motorway.

spots.name: Hodžovo námestie
spots.summary: Hodžovo námestie is a major square in Bratislava, the capital of Slovakia. The square is located at the edge of Old Town, in front of the Slovak Presidential Palace, some 5 minutes walking distance from the historical city center.

spots.name: Primate's Square
spots.summary: Primate's Square is a square situated in the middle of the Old Town of Bratislava, the capital of Slovakia. It is located between Slovak National Uprising Square and Main Square.

spots.name: Pálffy Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Pálffy Palace is a Baroque-style palace in the Old Town of Bratislava, on Ventúrska street. It was built by Count Leopold Pálffy in 1747. It has an interesting portal with a relief reflecting the military career of the count as a general in the army of Empress Maria Theresa.

spots.name: Chatam Sofer Memorial
spots.summary: Chatam Sofer Memorial, formerly the Old Jewish Cemetery is the burial place and memorial of Moses Sofer, a prominent orthodox rabbi from the 19th century, built on the site of a 17th-century Jewish cemetery in Bratislava, Slovakia.

spots.name: Maria Theresa monument
spots.summary: The Maria Theresa Monument was a monumental marble equestrian sculpture of the Hungarian Queen Maria Theresa made by the prominent Hungarian Presbyterian artist János Fadrusz, which stood on today's Ľudovít Štúr Square in Bratislava from 1897 to 1921.

spots.name: Laurinc Gate
spots.summary: Laurinc Gate was a medieval town gate in the historical Old Town of Bratislava, the capital of Slovakia. It was built in the 14th century and demolished by the order of Empress Maria Theresa of Austria in the 18th century together with most of the city walls, because the inner walls were limiting the town's growth.

spots.name: Heydukova Street Synagogue

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Heydukova Street Synagogue is an Orthodox congregation, synagogue, and Jewish museum, located on Heydukova Street in the Old Town of Bratislava, the capital of Slovakia. It is the only synagogue in Bratislava.

spots.name: Saint James's Chapel

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Saint James's Chapel is a ruined gothic chapel and surviving ossuary discovered underneath Námeste SNP in the center of Bratislava, Slovakia, in 1994. It is the oldest sacral medieval structure and the only ossuary in Bratislava.

spots.name: Botanical Garden of the Comenius University
spots.summary: Botanical Garden of the Comenius University is the only botanical garden in Bratislava, the capital of Slovakia. It is located in the Karlova Ves borough, next to the Old Town district and the Lafranconi Bridge by the Bratislava Riverfront and it contains over 4,000 plant species covering an area of 6.6 hectares.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Botanical Garden of the Comenius University

spots.name: Museum of Jewish Culture

hours.note: Closed Sat

spots.summary: The Museum of Jewish Culture is a museum in Bratislava, Slovakia, which focuses on the history of the Jews in Slovakia. Opened in 1993, it is a component of the Slovak National Museum, and its director is Pavol Mešťan.

names.fr: Musée de la culture juive de Bratislava

spots.name: University Library, Bratislava

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: University Library in Bratislava is the oldest library in Slovakia. It was founded in 1919 in Bratislava. Today, it is the largest and most visited library in Slovakia and it is a universal state research library.

names.ja: ブラチスラヴァ大学図書館

spots.name: Ľudovít Štúr Square
spots.summary: Ľudovít Štúr Square is a square in the Old Town district of Bratislava.

spots.name: Bratislava Transport Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Bratislava Transport Museum is a transport museum in Bratislava, Slovakia. It is a branch of the Slovak Technical Museum in Košice, is situated on the site of the first steam-railway station in Bratislava on Šancová Street, near the current main railway station in central Bratislava. It opened on June 24, 1999.

spots.name: Janko Kráľ Park
spots.summary: Janko Kráľ Park (Slovak: Sad Janka Kráľa, literally Janko Kráľ Orchard/Garden; formerly called Städtischer Aupark, is a park in Bratislava's Petržalka borough.

spots.name: Zochova
spots.summary: Zochova Street is a street in Bratislava's Old Town and Zochova is the name of a major bus stop in Bratislava, located at the point where the street touches Staromestská Street, next to Nový Most in Bratislava, Slovakia.

spots.name: Great Moravian Basilica in Bratislava

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Great Moravian Basilica in Bratislava was a Great Moravian church from 9th century at the Bratislava hillfort, in the area of current Bratislava Castle.

spots.name: Kapucínska Street
spots.summary: Kapucínska Street is a street in Bratislava, Slovakia in the historic center of the Old Town.

spots.name: Medical Garden
spots.summary: Medical Garden is a public park in Bratislava, Slovakia. It is located in the Old Town near the American square and behind the Aspremont Summer Palace.

spots.name: River Park
spots.summary: River Park is a mixed-use development on the river Danube in Old Town, Bratislava. It is a complex of administrative, residential, and commercial buildings developed by JTRE, and it includes the five-star Grand Hotel River Park.

spots.name: Lanfranconi Palace
spots.summary: Lanfranconi Palace or Lafranconi Palace is a neo-Renaissance representative bourgeois apartment house in Bratislava's Old Town, on the corner of Ludovita Štúr Square and Vajanského nábreží. The building was built in 1876-1877 by Ignác Feigler on the site of the former salt office.

spots.name: Trnavské mýto
spots.summary: Trnavské mýto is an important transport junction and crossroad in Bratislava, Slovakia, in the Nové Mesto district. It is located at 48°9′30″N 17°07′41″E.

spots.name: Aspremont Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Aspremont Summer Palace is a baroque palace in the Old Town of Bratislava, Slovakia. It was built along with the Medical Garden in 1770 for Count Johann Nepomuk Gobert d'Aspremont-Lynden. Nowadays the palace houses the office of the dean of the Faculty of Medicine of Comenius University.

spots.name: Holy Trinity Church, Podhradie

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Holy Trinity Church is a Roman Catholic church in Podhradie, a historical part of Bratislava, the capital of Slovakia situated underneath the Bratislava Castle next to the Danube riverbank.

spots.name: Palisády Street
spots.summary: Palisády Street is a major street in Bratislava's Old Town connecting Hodžovo námestie and Bratislava Castle in the Slovakia's capital. The street is served by public transport trolleybusses.

spots.name: Námestie Nežnej revolúcie
spots.summary: Námestie Nežnej revolúcie is a square in the Old Town borough of Bratislava adjacent to the SNP Square in front of the Old Market Hall.

spots.name: Red Bridge
spots.summary: Red Bridge is a railway bridge in Bratislava, Slovakia, spanning the Mlynská Valley. It is recognizable by its distinctive red paint and was built in 1848 as part of the Gänserndorf–Marchegg–Bratislava railway line and was originally single-track and built of red bricks. It was rebuilt to its current state in 1948.

spots.name: City Business Center

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: City Business Center is a complex of five office buildings in the Bratislava city district Staré mesto, first two finished in 2006 and 2007.

names.ja: シティー・ビジネス・センター・ブラチスラヴァ

spots.name: Slovak Radio Building
spots.summary: Its main building is a peculiar 60-m-high reversed pyramid from the communist era and a landmark in sharp contrast with the building of the Slovak National Bank just across the street.

spots.name: Slovak Pub

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: For good and reasonably priced halušky, the unique Slovak national meal, visit the Slovak Pub on Obchodna. This is a traditional eatery with a nice ambience. Portion size leans towards the small side. Not wheelchair accessible.

spots.name: Flagship

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Slovak national cuisine including halušky, in a converted theatre. Lacklustre service. Same company as Slovak Pub, who also own brewery Kláštorný pivovar, and café Franz Xaver Messerschmidt next door.

spots.name: Divný Janko Reštaurácia
spots.summary: Slovak and international dishes in a nice, retro ambience, the only downside is that the staff can be rude.

spots.name: San Marten

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: San Marten is an Italian restaurant with great food and excellent service at affordable prices.

hours.note: Closed Sat, Sun

spots.summary: Hare Krishna-operated restaurant popular with vegans and very affordable.

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: Communism-themed pub with high-quality beers and affordable prices.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Italian restaurant specializing in dishes from Veneto.
